b:
A journey
toward the roots
of my tree of time

The legs
of a fourth-year student
with a stethoscope round his neck
run backwards

Friends who ate and roamed together
and became one body
now stand as faces
I never knew

As a schoolboy
of the growing years,
when youthful desires
bloom and do not quite bloom

The white letters
on the blackboard
remind me of
the bitterness
of the computer screen

All the friendships
he lost
are within reach

In a torn
rubber shoe
a single pebble
beats time
on its own

The "royal intoxication"
of pen ink soaking
into fresh paper,
once again

The indecency
of "I love you"s
is now
a smile

Paper-ball cricket,
the kick-the-bottle game:
the boy who asked "why all this?"
is longing for them
today

To turn
all the petty quarrels
he started
into precious coins,

to snatch back a little
of the minutes he spent
with his sweetheart, the book,

to try out
the mischief he never did:

it is just a wish ..

Time laughs:
"While the wind is still blowing"
note: "While the wind is still blowing" is half of the proverb "winnow while there is wind": do things while you still can. "Petty quarrels into precious coins" plays on cellāk kācu (a worthless coin) and cellak kācu (a darling coin).
